title: Taxonomy of Rainfall Measures
note: Categories group specific rainfall variables according to the substantive feature of precipitation they measure rather than solely by units, aggregation period, or functional form. Variables measured over different temporal windows, such as monthly, seasonal, growing-season, or annual rainfall, remain in the same category when they capture the same substantive rainfall concept. Mathematical transformations are assigned separate categories when they change the substantive interpretation of the measure, as with deviations from normal, standardized anomalies, percentile measures, and one- or two-sided extreme events. Lagged rainfall measures are classified according to their underlying construction rather than assigned to a separate category. Cumulative or recurrent exposure remains distinct because it summarizes a history of rainfall shocks across multiple prior periods rather than a particular lagged realization. Named rainfall indices are distinguished from conventional standardized anomalies. Other is reserved for clearly identified and sufficiently specified measures that do not fit any predefined rainfall category, including identifiable non-rainfall measures. Unclassifiable is reserved for entries whose meaning or construction cannot be determined sufficiently from the extracted text and any supplied definition or context to assign a substantive rainfall category or establish that the measure falls outside the taxonomy. This includes unexplained codes, generic labels, incomplete fragments, uninterpretable or corrupted text, and rainfall measures with unspecified construction. A low classifier score alone does not determine either residual category.

categories.description: Raw accumulated precipitation over a specified period, rather than an average across observations or a historical reference period
Average precipitation across observations within a specified period, rather than accumulated precipitation or a long-run climatological mean
examples: Mean daily rainfall during the growing season
average monthly rainfall within a year
average rainfall during the current season

categories.description: Change in rainfall between periods rather than the contemporaneous rainfall level or departure from a climatological norm
examples: proportional change from the previous year

categories.description: Signed difference between realized rainfall and a historical or reference amount, expressed in rainfall units rather than percentages or standardized units
examples: rainfall deviation from a fitted trend

categories.description: Departure from normal expressed relative to the reference rainfall level rather than in rainfall units
examples: log rainfall minus log historical rainfall

categories.description: Continuous signed departure from normal expressed in units of the historical standard deviation, excluding separately defined named rainfall indices
Magnitude of departure from normal where the direction of the anomaly is intentionally removed, using absolute values or squared deviations
Position of realized rainfall within its historical distribution, without necessarily identifying an extreme event
Measures that jointly identify or categorize unusually wet and unusually dry realizations, rather than retaining only one tail of the rainfall distribution
examples: Above or below one standard deviation
below the 20th or above the 80th percentile

categories.description: Measures retaining only the lower tail of the rainfall distribution or rainfall deficits, including indicators and measures of deficit severity
Measures retaining only the upper tail of the rainfall distribution or rainfall surpluses, including indicators and measures of excess-rainfall severity
Number or frequency of days, months, or other observations experiencing rainfall, dryness, or a specified rainfall state, without measuring consecutive duration
examples: number of drought months in a year

categories.description: Persistence or consecutive duration of wet or dry conditions, rather than the total frequency of such conditions
Timing of the beginning, end, or arrival of rainfall or the rainy season, rather than the amount or frequency of precipitation
examples: start or end date of the rainy season

categories.description: Amount or maximum intensity of precipitation during a short event or interval, rather than an indicator of whether an extreme event occurred
Temporal concentration or uneven distribution of rainfall within a season or year, measured through the relative allocation of rainfall across intervals rather than its total amount
examples: Wettest-month rainfall relative to average rainfall
ratio of maximum monthly rainfall to average rainfall
share of seasonal rainfall occurring in the wettest month

categories.description: Statistical dispersion of rainfall across repeated observations or periods, rather than the temporal concentration of rainfall within a particular season
Named or composite precipitation-derived indices that transform or combine rainfall information using a specified index construction, including indices incorporating other hydroclimatic variables
Measures summarizing repeated rainfall shocks or accumulated exposure over multiple prior periods rather than a single rainfall realization from a particular period
examples: Number of droughts in the previous five or ten years
fraction of prior years classified as dry

categories.description: Historical or climatological rainfall conditions used directly as the measure of interest rather than solely as a reference for contemporaneous weather
examples: precipitation normal used as an instrument

categories.description: Persistent changes in rainfall conditions, including estimated trends and long-run shifts, rather than contemporaneous anomalies or year-to-year fluctuations

Clearly identified and sufficiently specified measures that do not fit any preceding rainfall category, including identifiable non-rainfall measures. Excludes entries whose meaning or construction is too incomplete or ambiguous to assess category fit.
examples: Covariance between monthly rainfall and monthly temperature

categories.description: Extracted strings that do not identify an interpretable measure, or that lack enough information about its construction to distinguish among the preceding rainfall categories. Includes gibberish, uninterpretable or corrupted text, unexplained codes or abbreviations, generic labels, and incomplete fragments when no supplied definition or context resolves their meaning.
examples: Rainfall with no indication of whether it is a total, mean, anomaly, or another measure
